question: Ticket a577fd03e307 says 'outline 6.6.3.7 claims the hostname only, implying OS-family publication is not required (stated via bounds.out rationale)', but outline 2.3.7.1.5 reads "System: a box has to name itself before any bus is up (a saveslate, an install), so the system device publishes the host's name and OS family (6.6.3.7). - akiendelllinux_cc_0 2.3.8Every device has the panes the base shim defines (17.1.3.5.2), drawn by the web server (15):" (Outline 2.3.7.1.5 states: 'the system device publishes the host's name and OS family'. The ticket's work only consolidates hostname retrieval calls. If built as written, the system device's published tool would satisfy only the hostname half of the requirement, leaving OS-family calls unconsolidated. The outline requires the system device to publish *both* as a unified system-identification interface; the ticket builds only the hostname half.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: Both stand; they do not conflict. Outline 6.6.3.7 has one exclusive clause, 'nothing else in Cairn asks the OS for the hostname', and that is exactly the call sites this ticket repoints. For OS family the outline says the system device answers it (6.6.3.7) and publishes it (2.3.7.1.5); it does: os_id() is in cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host, built by 5ccc7f05c932. Neither line says no other code may test the OS family, so the 54 OS-family checks are outside both the outline's exclusivity and this ticket's claim, and repointing them would be a new intention, not this one's missing half. Read from the whys already in the outline, so CC's (outline 0.4.1).
